header.title: Application Tracker
header.subtitle: Local scratch tracker and cover-letter renderer boundary, shown with fake demo data.

paragraphs: This public route shows fake data only. It documents the kind of local workflow used in ACB: tracked applications, generated artifact references, call cards, and keyword definitions.
The real local tracker writes under application-tracker/.private. The simple renderer remains a script workflow: application-tracker/letter.ps1 <slug>.

header.label: FOCUS / AGENTIC
header.title: Agentic systems
header.subtitle: Practical AI-assisted workflows, source-backed evidence, technical documentation, and reviewable outputs.

paragraphs: My work with AI-assisted systems focuses on useful boundaries: source-backed evidence, local/private data separation, reviewable artifacts, logs when they help, and human approval where outputs affect public or repository surfaces.

AgenticCareerBoost is the main artifact for this view. It also shows the correction history: earlier process machinery became too heavy, and the current repo keeps the useful evidence without treating the old harness as active law.

header.label: FOCUS / BACKEND
header.title: Backend and tooling
header.subtitle: Java/Spring base, domain rules, technical documentation, and platform-oriented work.

paragraphs: This view is for backend/platform conversations about behavior, boundaries, tooling, and maintainability. Java/Spring is part of the route, not the whole identity.
I am most interested in backend work when the domain has real shape: rules, transitions, permissions, failures, and enough complexity to reward clear structure.

IronBank shows the older backend thread. P3CTeX shows tooling and documentation depth. AAAAT is separate job-search tooling informed by the ACB scratch tracker. AgenticCareerBoost sits above them as public evidence where source, reports, local workflow boundaries, and checks have to stay aligned.
